headline: Intel's chief executive said Chinese AI models cost less to run, perform well enough and are being adopted very fast.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: the short Reuters report matches the headline, but it is one executive's remark with no figures behind it.
importance_line: The head of a major US chip maker saying Chinese models are cheap and good enough bears first on businesses choosing which AI to use, then on US and Chinese AI developers, then on chip makers such as Intel whose customers run these models; it is a remark at a panel, and no figures are given for the cost gap or the adoption.
summary: Reuters reports, as carried by The Economic Times, that Intel chief executive Lip-Bu Tan said at a panel organised by the bank DBS on Monday 12 Oct that Chinese frontier AI models (the most capable ones) have been cheaper per token, the small unit of text a model reads and writes and customers pay for, and that their adoption has been "very fast", calling the performance of models such as DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM "good enough". Tan, who said he is "a strong believer of open source" as "the best way to drive efficiency" and that markets will decide which models suit which uses, also said quantum computing could become mainstream within three to five years; Reuters gives no figures for the cost gap or the adoption.
notes: Reuters page blocked (401); read Reuters' text on The Economic Times (credited Reuters); url kept as Reuters' own link. Same DBS conference as the Broadcom (C05-05), DBS chief (C05-06) and TikTok (C05-09) items.
